learn.title: Grouping values
learn.body: So far each variable held one value. A struct groups several values, called fields, into one new type. A point has an x and a y, a person has a name and an age. The fields sit next to each other in memory.

learn.title: Defining and copying
learn.body: This prints `3 4` and then `3 9`. A dot reaches a field. Assigning `b = a` copies every field, so changing `b.y` leaves `a` alone.

learn.title: Through a pointer
learn.body: With a pointer to a struct, use the arrow `->`. `p->x` means `(*p).x`. This function changes the caller's struct, so calling `shift(&a)` makes `a.x` 13.

learn.title: Size of a struct
learn.body: `struct point` holds two ints. How big is it here?
steps: Some structs get padding bytes, so use `sizeof`

learn.body: Passing a struct to a function copies all of it. Passing a pointer copies only the address, which is cheaper for big structs.

questions.prompt: Use the \_\_ operator to reach a field of a struct variable.
questions.explanation: `a.x` reads the field x of the struct variable a.

questions.prompt: Which reaches a field through a pointer `p`?
questions.explanation: The arrow follows the pointer and picks the field.

questions.prompt: `struct point b = a;` then `b.y = 9;`. What happens to `a.y`?
questions.explanation: `b` is a separate copy, so a is unchanged.

questions.prompt: `struct point` has two ints. How many bytes is it on our platform?
`a.x` is 3 and we call `shift(&a)` which adds 10. What is `a.x`?
questions.explanation: The function changes the caller's struct through the pointer.
Dereference the pointer first, then pick the field.

questions.prompt: Match each piece to its meaning.
questions.explanation: Structs act like single values with parts inside.
